correctness.rationale: The continuous-time generator gives exact first and second moment equations under exchangeability; their solved rational expressions agree with an independently computed exact stationary count-chain for 12 test cases. Symbolic differentiation gives the displayed quartic with exactly one positive simple root by Descartes. Sign and tail arguments imply strict global uniqueness. Scaling r=c/sqrt(m), root bracketing and substitution prove the optimizer and maximum asymptotics; the explicit positive rational identity proves strict finite ceiling. Finite experiments are not used as universal proof. The analytic identity and parameter edges were independently recalculated.

originality.rationale: The general zealot-voter discord equations and qualitative polarization are already published by Vendeville–Zhou–Guedj (arXiv:2203.02002) and not newly claimed. The assessed global optimizer and sharp asymptotics require the explicit derivative polynomial, positive-root uniqueness, and limit analysis; relevant full primary-paper sections and published-result searches revealed no equivalent or stronger cover. Gastner–Ishida has a superficially analogous m^(3/2) scaling but for a different consensus-time model. Residual priority uncertainty is acknowledged, not treated as a proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The foundational general graph pair equations allow the present finite formulas by direct specialization, so priority rests on the precise global optimizer/ceiling/asymptotics rather than solving the pair system.

Search ranking is incomplete and nonreturn alone does not certify novelty.

value.rationale: Within-community discord is a natural observable measure of cohesive-cluster fragmentation in the motivating voter dynamics. Knowing whether extra cross-group mixing increases or decreases this quantity, exactly where it peaks, and its irreducible sharp ceiling addresses the reported nonmonotonicity with a complete all-size theorem rather than a routine numerical instance. The simultaneous monotone decline of mean-opinion polarization establishes a substantive distinction between aggregate polarization and internal group diversity. The sharp m^(-1/2) optimal rate provides a scaling benchmark.
